name: AzureBlobPut
caption: Azure Blob: Upload file

configuration.description: Code of an AutoFlow Credential (max 20 chars; longer values are cut, matching is not case-sensitive). Its authentication type must be 'OAuth 2.0 client credentials' (Entra app, scope https://storage.azure.com/.default) or 'Azure Storage SAS token'. Credentials are company data and are NOT part of the flow definition – the code must exist in the target company.

Storage account name (3-24 lowercase letters/digits), e.g. contosodocs for https://contosodocs.blob.core.windows.net. Trimmed. May contain SmartFields; the resolved value is checked when the step runs.
Blob container name (3-63 chars, lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens, starting/ending with letter or digit; $root and $web also accepted). Trimmed. SmartFields allowed.
Target path inside the container, e.g. invoices/{{trigger_Rec.no}}.pdf. Folders are implicit. Trimmed, backslashes become slashes, a leading slash is dropped. Must not end with '/'.

What to upload. If the raw value is exactly one SmartField (e.g. {{CreatePdf_Document}}) that names an AutoFlow Document reference, that document's bytes are uploaded and its content type is used; if it is one field of a record reference (e.g. {{trigger_Rec.picture}}) that is a BLOB, Media or MediaSet field, its bytes are uploaded. Anything else is resolved as SmartText and uploaded as UTF-8 text, including a binary HTTP Request responseBody (its base64 text is uploaded, not the bytes).
MIME type stored with the blob. Empty = the source document's content type, else derived from the file extension of path.
Replace an existing blob with the same path. When false the step first checks for an exact-path match and fails if it exists.

Index tags written with the blob: array of {"name": string, "value": string} (max 10). value supports SmartText. Rows with an empty name are dropped by the editor; at run time an empty name fails the tag-name check.

rules.check: configuration.credentialCode must be non-empty. The editor marks the field as required ("Please fill in the highlighted fields."); at run time an empty code fails the step with this message.
rules.message: Select a credential for the Azure Blob Storage connection.

rules.check: The credential must exist in the company. Also shown as an advisory on the editor's status line (prefixed with ⚠); it does not block saving.
The credential's authentication type must be 'OAuth 2.0 client credentials' or 'Azure Storage SAS token'. Also shown as an advisory on the editor's status line (prefixed with ⚠).
rules.message: Credential %1 uses the authentication type "%2". Azure Blob Storage steps accept "%3" (an Entra app) or "%4".

rules.check: Editor status line only (advisory, prefixed with ⚠, does not block saving): an OAuth 2.0 client-credentials credential's scope should contain 'storage.azure.com'. Not checked at run time; a wrong scope surfaces as an Azure authentication error.
rules.message: Credential %1 requests the scope "%2". Azure Blob Storage needs a token for the scope https://storage.azure.com/.default.

rules.check: The resolved storageAccount (trimmed) must be 3-24 chars of a-z and 0-9; an empty value also fails. Checked when the step runs, before any Azure call. The editor does not check the format. The machine check skips values containing '{{'.
rules.message: The storage account name "%1" is not valid. It must be 3 to 24 characters long and contain only lowercase letters and digits.

rules.check: The resolved container (trimmed) must be $root, $web, or 3-63 chars of a-z, 0-9 and single hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen; an empty value also fails. Checked when the step runs. The editor does not check the format. The machine check skips values containing '{{'.
rules.message: The container name "%1" is not valid. It must be 3 to 63 characters long and contain only lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

rules.check: A SAS-token credential must have a token stored.
rules.message: Credential %1 has no SAS token stored.

rules.check: If the credential has base URLs (an allow-list), https://<storageAccount>.blob.core.windows.net/<container> must start with one of them. Also shown as an advisory on the editor status line when account and container are literal.
rules.message: The URL "%1" is not allowed by credential "%2". Allowed prefixes: %3.

rules.check: The resolved path (after trimming, backslash->slash, leading slash removed) must be non-empty. The editor marks the field as required ("Please fill in the highlighted fields.").
rules.message: Enter the path of the file, for example invoices/2026/INV-1001.pdf.

rules.check: The normalized resolved path must not end with '/'. Not checked in the editor.
rules.message: The path "%1" ends with a slash, so it names a folder. Enter the path of a file.

rules.check: At most 10 entries in tags. Checked when the step runs, before the upload. Not checked in the editor.
rules.message: A file can have at most 10 index tags; %1 are configured.

rules.check: Tag names (trimmed) must be unique. Checked when the step runs. The editor's tag column also refuses a duplicate name.
rules.message: The index tag "%1" is configured more than once.

rules.check: Each tag name (trimmed) must be 1-128 characters. Checked when the step runs.
rules.message: The index tag name "%1" is not valid. It must be 1 to 128 characters long.

rules.check: Each resolved tag value must be at most 256 characters. Checked when the step runs, after SmartFields are resolved.
rules.message: The value of index tag "%1" is too long. Tag values can have at most 256 characters.

rules.check: Tag names and resolved values may only contain letters a-z/A-Z, digits 0-9, space and + - . / : = _. Checked when the step runs, after SmartFields are resolved.
rules.message: The index tag "%1" contains the character "%2". Tag names and values may only contain letters, digits, spaces and the characters + - . / : = _

rules.check: The resolved content must not be empty (zero bytes).
rules.message: The content of the file is empty. Check the Content field – a SmartField there may not have resolved.

rules.check: overwrite = false and a blob with exactly this path exists.
rules.message: The file %1 already exists in container %2. Turn on "Overwrite existing file" to replace it.

notes: A binary HTTP Request responseBody reaches this step as base64 text, so {{<slug>_responseBody}} uploads the base64, not the file. To upload the file, store it in a BLOB or Media field with Insert/Modify Record first and use that field.
url is https://<storageAccount>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<path> (no SAS appended). size is the uploaded byte count. name is the last path segment.

Tags are sent URL-encoded as the blob's index tags in the same upload request. Writing tags needs Storage Blob Data Owner (or a SAS with the Tags permission); uploading needs Storage Blob Data Contributor. With overwrite = false the existence check also needs list permission.
Tag character check: only ASCII letters a-z/A-Z count as letters; umlauts and other non-ASCII letters are rejected.

Azure error codes are translated: BlobNotFound ('The file %1 was not found in container %2 of storage account %3.'), ContainerNotFound ('The container %1 was not found in storage account %2.'), Authorization* ('Azure denied access to container %1 (%2). The Entra app needs the role Storage Blob Data Reader to list and download, Storage Blob Data Contributor to upload, and Storage Blob Data Owner to read or write index tags; a SAS token needs the matching permissions. Azure answered: %3'), AuthenticationFailed/InvalidAuthenticationInfo/NoAuthenticationInformation ('Azure could not authenticate the request (%1). For an Entra app, check that the credential uses the scope https://storage.azure.com/.default; for a SAS token, check that it has not expired. Azure answered: %2'); anything else becomes 'Uploading the file failed: <Azure text>'.

There is no publish-time check for this step. In the editor only the required fields (credentialCode, storageAccount, container, path, content) and the advisory status line (credential exists, type, OAuth scope, URL allow-list) apply; every other check runs when the step runs.
